name: MS-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+21 partisan lean strongly favors Republicans
Incumbent Mike Ezell running with a large fundraising edge
Democrat Jeffrey Hulum raised under $30,000 with no outside spending
Prediction markets price Democratic chances near 3%
model.rationale: The R+21 district, Ezell's incumbency, and his roughly 34-to-1 fundraising advantage over Hulum leave the Democrat without a visible path; markets price his chances at about 3%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, pointing to a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: A major outside-spending intervention on Hulum's behalf or a scandal involving Ezell would be the only realistic route to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Mississippi's 4th District is deeply Republican territory, with a partisan lean of R+21, and first-term incumbent Mike Ezell is seeking reelection after easily securing his party's nomination. Ezell has raised nearly $1 million for the cycle, giving him a dominant financial position over his rivals.

Democratic nominee Jeffrey Hulum has raised under $30,000 and reports only about $6,500 on hand, with no outside spending on either side. Independent Carl Boyanton is also on the ballot but lacks the resources to be a factor. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, and prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 3% chance. All available evidence points to a decisive Ezell victory in November.
